title.narrative: Caritas Marsabit Agroecology & Climate Resilience Learning Journey

description.narrative:
The Agroecology & Climate Resilience Learning Journey is a three-year initiative (2026-2029) implemented by Caritas Marsabit in Kenya's arid Marsabit County. Part of a CAFOD programme with eight partners, this project generates longitudinal evidence linking agroecological practices to climate resilience outcomes among smallholder farmers.
Marsabit faces recurrent droughts and land degradation. While Caritas Marsabit promotes agroecological interventions (composting, water harvesting, FMNR), systematic evidence connecting these practices to measurable resilience outcomes in ASAL contexts is limited. This Learning Journey addresses that gap.
Over three years, 100+ farmers (50% women) engaged in Caritas Marsabit livelihoods projects will be surveyed at baseline, midline, and endline. The participatory methodology utilizes the FAO Tool for Agroecology Performance Evaluation (TAPE), co-designed with partners, complemented by resilience indicators (livelihood diversification, adaptive capacity, food security). Digital data collection via KOBO Collect ensures accuracy.
With a budget of £7,750, funds support data collection, training, travel, and analysis. The project strengthens Caritas Marsabit's internal MEAL systems. Managed by senior staff, the initiative ensures financial stewardship through established systems and environmental stewardship via digital tools and optimized travel.
Academic collaboration with BOKU University enhances methodological rigor. Findings will inform programming, scale practices, and support advocacy at county and global levels. Thematic standards prioritize gender inclusion, ethical data collection, and environmental sustainability. Ultimately, this journey empowers Caritas Marsabit to demonstrate how agroecology builds climate resilience, contributing to global advocacy and policy engagement.
